page.layout: One column of verse, seven stanzas, from top to bottom. Below the last stanza, at the right, a gathering signature. Running head at top centre, page number at top right. No margin notes.

main_text.p: Evertit ausus, & variat vices. Hoc fracta hebescunt spicula fortium, Hoc debiles firmantur artus Robore non patiente vinci.
Largo repleti qui fuerant cibo, Victum ob parandum nunc operas locant: Et qui fame contra peribant, Nunc nimio saturantur esu.
Tædas inanes, & sterilem thorum Qua expostulabat, nunc sobole affluit: Quæque affluebat, nunc minuti Damna gemit miseranda lecti.
Vitæ necisq; est unicus arbiter Creator orbis: cum lubet horrido Detrudit Orco, mox reducit (Cùm lubet) æthereas in auras.
Dites oborta pauperie obruit, Amplis egenos divitiis beat, Nunc deprimit summum tenentes, Nunc humiles super astra mittit.
Sape infimo de pulvere pauperem Ad celsa rerum culmina provehit, Virisque summis assidentem In solio statuit supremo.
Immensa terræ qui sola fulciunt, Torquentur eius Numine cardines, Quibus super vasti locauit Templa opifex speciosa cæli.

page.notes: No marginal notes, no catchword, no reference marks. The printed page number 229 is at top right and the running head is at top centre. The signature P. iij. is at the lower right. Some letters are blurred in the scan, especially the stanza openers (Euertit, Tædas, Sape, Dites), so the readings Evertit, Tædas and Sape are the likely ones, not certain. The Greek-style ligatures in Tædas and Quæque are read as æ. Long s is written as plain s throughout.
